text:
eve.customer: hitting intermittent 502s from our prod app when it talks to internal-mgmt.redwood.svc via the VPC endpoint. Started ~0900 UTC, about 10% of requests failing with TLS errors. can someone triage?

alice.support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a curl + error and a small dig/nslookup output so we can see what it's resolving to?

eve.customer: sample: `curl -v --resolve internal-mgmt.redwood.svc:443:10.2.5.11 https://internal-mgmt.redwood.svc/api/health` returns 200. but `curl -v https://internal-mgmt.redwood.svc/api/health` intermittently fails with `SSL: certificate subject name 'prod.redwood.ai' doesn't match target 'internal-mgmt.redwood.svc'` (curl exit 35). `dig internal-mgmt.redwood.svc +short` sometimes returns `10.2.5.11` and sometimes `3.4.5.6`.

alice.support: that looks like split-horizon leakage — the name is resolving to a public IP (3.4.5.6) intermittently which explains the cert mismatch. do you have any customers/VPCs with cross-account hosted zones?

ben.platform: pinging in — can you also paste `kubectl get pods -n platform -o wide` for a sample node or list of node-local-dns pods? node-local caches can hold stale answers and cause flips like this. also, do `dig @<node-local-ip> internal-mgmt.redwood.svc +trace` on a node.

eve.customer: node-local dns is running on nodes. here's quick dig sequences from pod exec:
```$ dig internal-mgmt.redwood.svc +short
10.2.5.11
$ dig internal-mgmt.redwood.svc +short
3.4.5.6
```

carol.network: I queried Route53 for that name across our accounts. found two hosted zones with the same zone name: hz-0a1b2c (private, acct A) and hz-9f8e7d (private, acct B) — acct B's zone is NOT associated with this VPC, but acct A's zone is associated. However there is also a public hosted zone (hz-public-xyz) with a CNAME pointing internal-mgmt -> prod-frontend.redwood.ai which resolves to 3.4.5.6. in some resolver flows the public zone answer is leaking through when the resolver falls back to the global resolver.

alice.support: interesting. that can happen when resolver rule/forwarder priorities or VPC associations are inconsistent, or when node-local TTLs expire and the client falls back to an external resolver. can you confirm the VPC associations and resolver rule priorities?

carol.network: checked: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-0a2b3c` shows an association to a forwarder in acct X with priority default. There's also a conditional forwarder for the zone in acct B that isn't associated. tl;dr: some resolver paths hit the public/inconsistent zone. also found node-local `cache-size` low and TTL set to 60s on the pod, which can make flips visible to clients.

ben.platform: here's a reproduction plan: 1) exec into a workload pod and run `dig internal-mgmt.redwood.svc` repeatedly to watch flips; 2) restart `nodelocaldns` daemonset (or `kubectl rollout restart ds/nodelocaldns`) to clear caches; 3) temporarily add an allowlist entry for the public IP in egress firewall so that requests that resolve to 3.4.5.6 don't get dropped while we fix DNS.

alice.support: mitigation steps for customer: 1) Associate the correct private hosted zone (hz-0a1b2c) to the VPC if missing. 2) Remove/disable the public CNAME pointing internal-mgmt -> prod-frontend or make it conditional. 3) Restart node-local DNS to clear stale cache. 4) If relying on Route53 resolver rules across accounts, ensure the conditional forwarder is associated and has higher priority than the default forwarder.

eve.customer: thumbs up. i associated hz-0a1b2c to the VPC and restarted node-local. after that we saw steady responses to 10.2.5.11 and TLS errors stopped. thanks.

carol.network: follow-up: we found the root cause was a CI job creating a public CNAME for the same name during a deploy in acct B (bad infra-as-code template). i've opened a PR to prevent publishing that CNAME for internal names and a playbook to check for duplicate zone names across accounts.

dns-bot: automated-detect: duplicate-zone-name detected: internal-mgmt.redwood.svc present in hz-9f8e7d (acct-b) and hz-public-xyz. Recommended action: mark internal-only names as private in IaC and block public zone creation for matching patterns.

alice.support: closing loop — customer confirmed recovery, tracking owners: carol.network to follow up on IaC PR, ben.platform to add a node-local cache check to the runbook, alice.support to update support KB with steps and quick mitigations. feel free to re-open if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
